summary: Fixed the revision-2 trust defect Director review found: gate-pr in .github/workflows/relay-merge-gate.yml now triggers on pull_request_target instead of pull_request, so its workflow definition is always sourced from the trusted base branch (main) rather than from the PR under evaluation. For a same-repo PR (every Relay worker branch), GitHub sources a pull_request-triggered run's workflow YAML from the PR branch itself; a worker PR could therefore have rewritten this gate's own logic and used its statuses: write permission to publish its own passing relay-merge-gate status regardless of what state.json actually said. pull_request_target closes that because the workflow definition is always the base-branch copy, independent of the PR. The job is otherwise unchanged from revisions 1/2 and stays within the authorized boundary: it checks out only the PR's base commit (never the PR head), never executes or imports PR-supplied code, and reads PR number/head SHA/title solely from event metadata passed through env (never interpolated into the script body). gate-refresh (push to main touching .ai-ops/state.json, republishing the same relay-merge-gate status for every open [RELAY ...] PR) is unchanged from revision 2. The shared evaluateMergeGate/planRefreshStatuses invariant, its fixtures, and relay-automerge.yml/relay-fastlane.yml are unchanged. Added a new static self-test (checkWorkflowTrustBoundary) that re-parses the checked-in workflow file to confirm gate-pr still triggers on pull_request_target and its checkout step still pins base.sha rather than the PR head, plus a fixture covering the null/malformed-state fail-closed case, so a future regression fails CI instead of silently reopening the hole.
root_cause_evidence: Revision 2's root cause is confirmed unchanged and re-verified in this run: PP-RELAY-057 PR #104 and PP-RELAY-058 PRs #105/#106 merged to main while state.json still recorded a pre-approval status (merged_by on all three is the repository owner's own account, not relay-automerge.yml's automation, and none carry its forced '[RELAY <task>] Director-approved squash merge' commit title) -- GitHub permits any account with merge rights to squash-merge an open, green, non-draft PR directly regardless of state.json, and only a required-status-check branch protection rule can prevent that. This run additionally re-fetched PR #108's commit status directly (GET /repos/palmistrypath/palmistry-site/commits/d11e4ae46d4b8fbfe15062a8544f41221d389c2f/status via the pull_request_read get_status method): total_count is 0, confirming the task packet's claim that gate-pr never actually ran to completion on that PR, so the revision-2 trust defect was never exploited or exercised as a passing/failing required check in production -- it was caught by Director diff review, not by a failed live signal. PR #108's full diff was inspected (55.9 KB) to confirm exactly what revision 2 added (gate-refresh, planRefreshStatuses, five refresh fixtures) versus what revision 1 already had (gate-pr, evaluateMergeGate, seven single-PR fixtures) before making the trigger-only change.
design_correction: Changed exactly one property of gate-pr's trigger: `on: pull_request_target` (with the same event types -- opened, reopened, synchronize, edited, ready_for_review -- and the same `branches: [main]` scope) in place of `on: pull_request`, plus `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'` to match. No other job logic, permission, checkout ref, or script call changed. verify-relay-merge-gate.mjs and publish-relay-merge-gate-status.mjs are otherwise identical to revision 2 (only comments/usage text updated to say pull_request_target instead of pull_request); evaluateMergeGate, planRefreshStatuses, and all 12 revision-2 fixtures are byte-for-byte unchanged. Added one new fixture (08-null-state-fails-closed.json, state: null) and one new self-test function, checkWorkflowTrustBoundary, which statically parses .github/workflows/relay-merge-gate.yml's gate-pr job body and fails if: the job's `if:` condition is not exactly `github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'`; the workflow's `on:` block contains a bare `pull_request:` trigger key; the `on:` block lacks `pull_request_target:`; any actions/checkout step in the job references `head.sha`/`head.ref`; or no checkout step pins `base.sha`. Manually verified this check fails (with the exact expected problem messages) when gate-pr's trigger is reverted to pull_request or its checkout ref is pointed at head.sha, and passes on the final committed file.

Manual regression proof: temporarily reverted gate-pr's `if:` and `on:` to pull_request -- workflow-trust-boundary self-test correctly FAILed with the three expected problem messages; restored the committed file and re-ran -- PASS again

Manual regression proof: temporarily pointed the gate-pr checkout `ref:` at github.event.pull_request.head.sha -- workflow-trust-boundary self-test correctly FAILed (head-checkout + missing-base.sha problems); restored and re-ran -- PASS again

Not verified: an actual live GitHub Actions run of gate-pr under pull_request_target reacting to a real PR, since that requires either the human owner's branch-protection change already applied or opening a live PR against this task's own branch -- both outside this task's authorized scope. The pull_request_target vs pull_request workflow-sourcing behavior this fix relies on is GitHub's documented, well-established trigger semantics, not a claim requiring a live experiment to establish; the fixture tests, static self-test, and CLI dry runs above are the closest bounded proof available to this worker.

Also enable 'Do not allow bypassing the above settings' (including for administrators) on that same rule, since the account that performed the PP-RELAY-057/-058 out-of-band merges has merge rights on main and would otherwise still be able to bypass a required check. execution.notes: This revision changes only the trust boundary of the PR-side status publication (pull_request -> pull_request_target); the underlying merge-authorization invariant, its 12 inherited fixtures, the push-triggered refresh path, and relay-automerge.yml/relay-fastlane.yml are all byte-for-byte or logic-for-logic unchanged from the closed revision-2 PR #108. No live GitHub Actions execution of the new trigger was observed by this worker (see the 'Not verified' verification entry); this is disclosed rather than overstated.
